entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text:
Since both aforesaid miscellaneous appeals filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are arising out of common award dated 9 th of August, 2011 passed by Additional Member,
MACT(FTC), Mandsaur in Claim Case No.78 of 2010, therefore, they are heard together and disposed of by this common order.

(2) MA No.2956 of 2011 has been filed by claimants seeking enhancement of compensation amount whereas, MA No.2667 of 2011 has been filed by Insurance Company seeking reduction of compensation amount awarded by Claims Tribunal.

(3) Briefly stated the facts of the case are that on 23-01-2009 around 1:30 am, 2 MA 2956 of 2011 and MA 2667 of 2011 Ankit Minda (since deceased) was going with his friend Anukul Verma in a Hyundai Car bearing registration No.MP-09-HD-2667 and the said car was being driven by deceased Anukul Verma in a very rash and negligent manner as a result of which it dashed a tree and one Lalit Rathore died on spot.
Claimants who are father, mother and minor brother of deceased filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.22,60,000/- before Claims Tribunal.
The Insurance Company also filed reply to claim petition denying averments of claimants.

sentences.text: (4) On the basis of pleadings of both the parties and documents available therein, Claims Tribunal framed issues and awarded compensation of Rs.4,34,500/- along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization in favour of claimants.
(5) Challenging the impugned Award, learned Counsel for claimants submits that Claims Tribunal has grossly erred in not awarding just and reasonable compensation.

At the time of accident,
deceased was a bachelor, aged around 22 years and was working as Sales Executive in HDFC Bank and also, pursuing his studies of MBA.
His future was very bright.
The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not taking into consideration future prospects.

Learned Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of deceased despite the fact that he was receiving perks and incentives besides salary and proper multiplier has not been applied by Claims Tribunal.
Claimants are totally dependent on the deceased.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation amount.

On the other hand, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company submits that as per salary certificate Ex.P6, the deceased was earning Rs.4,500/- per month because of the fact that deceased was a temporary employee.
Additional of Rs.2,500/- was paid for other expenses of deceased which should not be included by the Claims Tribunal while assessing the income of deceased.
The Claims Tribunal ought to have considered testimony of PW3- Gopal in proper perspective who has clearly stated about income of deceased.
The Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation on the higher side.
The Claims Tribunal has wrongly affixed liability on the Insurance Company without giving weight to the evidence available on record.
(7) Heard learned Counsel for parties.
Perused record as well as impugned Award.
(8) So far as the question of quantum of compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal is concerned, no such credible statement has been produced on record by the Insurance Company

that as per payslip,
deceased Ankit has not been appointed in HDFC Bank as temporary employee.

From the statement of father of deceased Vinod, it is found proved that Ankit is getting a salary of Rs.7,000/- per month by working in HDFC Bank whereby Claims Tribunal has given a finding in this regard.

Although the deceased was not in Government servant but looking to educational qualification and bright future of the deceased, 40% towards future prospect ought to have applied by the Claims Tribunal in the light of decision of Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Pranay Sethi, 4 MA 2956 of 2011 and MA 2667 of 2011 reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 and the claimants are entitled for future prospect 40%.

,
multiplier of 18 should be applied.
Besides aforesaid, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of consortium, a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

Accordingly, claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-

2  40% towards future prospect  Multiplier 18 (Rs.7,000/-+40%FP-1/2 x12x18) 
 Other heads:-
 Loss of filial consortium  (father, mother and brother of deceased) 
 Loss of estate   Loss of expenses
Tota (9)
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.12,08,400/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.4,34,500/-.
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.7,73,900/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

(10) With aforesaid modification, miscellaneous appeal filed by claimants is disposed of by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.7,73,900/- The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims 5 MA 2956 of 2011 and MA 2667 of 2011 Tribunal.

If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.

Thereafter,
the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
(11) In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the Insurance Company fails and is hereby dismissed.
A copy of this order be placed in connected MA No. 2667 of 2011.
